title: Ansel and the Inheritance
premise: When Rafael Okonkwo, the meticulous coroner of Hollowmere, supervises the ceremonial exhumation of town founder Edmund Ansel for the bicentennial, the coffin proves empty—except for a brass ledger keyed to the graves Rafael has tended for twenty years. Decoding it reveals that Ansel's fortune was built on trafficking, and that certain founding families have been paying 'inheritance dues' ever since, burying anyone who asked questions in plots only Rafael would recognize. As Rafael traces the ledger's cipher through headstones and parish records, they realize the current heirs intend to make them the next entry. The story ends with Rafael choosing to publish the ledger rather than destroy it, dismantling the town's quiet economy of silence at the cost of their own anonymity—and standing at last over a grave bearing their own name, carved before they could stop it.
about_author: Rosalind Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing small-town archives across New England before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about paper trails, buried ledgers, and the people who keep other people's secrets.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Every Grave
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establishes Hollowmere's bicentennial preparations and Rafael's ritualized, alphabetized care of the cemetery—a life built on invisibility after an unspoken early grief. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as devotion.

chapters.title: Order of Exhumation
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A court order arrives: founder Edmund Ansel must be exhumed for DNA verification tied to an inheritance dispute filed by an outsider named Vera Lindqvist. Mayor Colton Hale pressures Rafael to handle it quietly. Beat: first crack in the routine.

chapters.title: Empty Brass
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, witnessed by Hale and Lindqvist. The coffin opens on no body—only a sealed brass ledger wedged beneath the lining. Hale orders the site closed; Lindqvist photographs everything. Beat: cold shock, professional composure fraying.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Plots
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At night Rafael studies the ledger: columns of plot numbers, dates, and sums, cross-referenced to burials Rafael personally performed—including three ruled accidental deaths. Beat: dread as the familiar becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Vera Lindqvist Claims a Grandmother
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Vera, who reveals her grandmother vanished in Hollowmere in 1974; the inheritance suit was her lever to force an exhumation. She and Rafael form an uneasy alliance. Beat: wary kinship between outsiders.

chapters.title: The Dues
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Decoded entries show annual payments from five founding families into an account still active—the 'Ansel Inheritance Fund,' administered by Hale's bank. Someone has been paying for fifty years. Beat: the past is present tense.

chapters.title: Grave Seven-Teen
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Plot 7-T holds not the recorded occupant but an unidentified man buried in 1998—the year Rafael's predecessor died suddenly. Rafael realizes their own records were edited before they inherited the job. Beat: guilt and vertigo.

chapters.title: A Warning in Alphabetical Order
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael finds the office files reordered overnight, their name moved to the front of the burial registry—an elegant threat from someone who knows their systems intimately. Beat: paranoia; the watcher is inside.

chapters.title: Deputy Bright
chapters.summary: Deputy Naomi Bright's POV. She's investigating a missing hiker whose last GPS ping was near the cemetery. Her parallel inquiry nearly exposes Rafael's midnight digging. Beat: tension between procedure and secrecy.

chapters.title: The Founders' Dinner
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the bicentennial gala, Rafael works the room: Hale deflects, matriarch Eugenia Ansel-Croft quotes scripture about debts, and archivist Peter Munn goes pale when Rafael mentions plot 7-T. Beat: masked hostility, social chess.

chapters.title: What Happened to Munn
chapters.summary: Bright's POV. Archivist Peter Munn is found drowned in the reservoir days after speaking with Rafael—ruled accidental by the county. Rafael recognizes the signature staging. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Stones
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael cracks the ledger's final layer: epitaph initials across twenty graves spell out names of the trafficked and murdered, including Vera's grandmother. Beat: triumph curdling into horror at the scale.

chapters.title: Eugenia's Confession, Partially
chapters.summary: Eugenia Ansel-Croft's POV. She admits the family took 'dues' to protect the town's reputation but claims she doesn't know who enforces collection now—or where Edmund's body went. Beat: complicity dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Chapel Road
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael is run off the road returning from the county archive with microfilm; the film is stolen, and a note left in its place lists Rafael's sister's address. Beat: fear becomes personal.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger Too
chapters.summary: Bright's POV. Following bank records, Bright discovers Hale has been skimming the fund for years—he needs the exhumation scandal buried more than anyone. She hesitates to trust Rafael with it. Beat: alliances tested by ambition.

chapters.title: The Room Beneath the Mausoleum
chapters.summary: Rafael and Vera's POV, alternating. Following ledger coordinates, they break into the Ansel mausoleum and find a sub-cellar: Edmund's remains, boxes of records, and a modern cot—someone has been keeping watch there recently. Beat: revelation and pursuit; they flee as headlights arrive.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, flashback interleaved with present. It emerges that Rafael's predecessor—and Rafael's own mentor—was the collector, and trained Rafael unknowingly to maintain the system. Beat: devastating self-reckoning; innocence lost retroactively.

chapters.title: The Collector Named
chapters.summary: Bright's POV. Evidence converges on Sheriff's coroner liaison Douglas Wrenn, who inherited the collector role and has been eliminating loose ends—Munn, the hiker, soon Rafael. But Wrenn has county protection. Beat: the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Deadline at Dawn
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Wrenn offers Rafael the mentor's old chair: keep filing, stay invisible, live. He gives them until sunrise to hand over the original ledger. Beat: temptation of comfortable complicity.

chapters.title: Exhumation, Second Order
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Rafael's POV. Instead of surrendering the ledger, Rafael files emergency exhumation paperwork naming all twenty plots, forcing public excavation under press presence as Wrenn moves to stop it. Beat: courage as paperwork; the pen against the shovel.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gives Up
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Multiple POVs converge at the cemetery. Wrenn attempts to burn the records vault; Bright arrests him mid-act; Eugenia publicly confirms the fund's origin; Hale resigns. Rafael reads the carved names aloud over open graves. Beat: catharsis, justice outside and inside the law at once.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Resolution. Rafael's POV. Months later: trials proceed, Vera reclaims her grandmother's remains, and Rafael—no longer anonymous—tends a new stone bearing their own name, which Wrenn had commissioned as a threat and Rafael keeps as a reminder. Beat: survival's price paid willingly; visibility chosen.
